text:
maria: Quick question — if region-eu gets evicted and we failover traffic to region-us in an active/active event, how do we ensure EU-resident PII tenants never get executed on a US quantized model? legal explicitly forbids cross-border execution for those tenants.
ken: Short answer: we shouldn't. We need a clear fail-closed path for PII-tagged tenants.
devon: Options: keep standby capacity in EU, route PII tenants to hosted EU dedicated pool, or return an explicit error and surface degradation to the app.
ashley: Note: there's also a model-variant mismatch risk. EU currently serves int8-q, US serves int4-q — outputs differ, but legal cares about data locality not numeric drift.
jon: Proposal: add a residency routing policy that checks tenant.residency tag and does one of: (a) reject with 503+explain, (b) route to residency-only fallback pool (unquantized CPU or dedicated EU), (c) proxy to customer-managed private deployment in-region.
maria: Is returning 503 acceptable for product? For high-sensitivity tenants we can degrade, product said yes for some SLAs but not all. We need tenant-level policy.
ken: Implementation principle: default to best-effort for untagged tenants; fail-closed for tenants flagged "eu-pii". This requires tenant metadata + enforcement at proxy.
devon: Implementation sketch for proxy rules:
```
if tenant.residency == 'eu-pii' && current_region != 'eu':
  return 503, 'residency_fallback'
elif current_region == 'eu':
  route_normal()
else:
  route_best_effort_variant()
```
ashley: Ops concern — during chaos tests operator needs clear metrics/traces to see how many requests got rejected vs routed. Otherwise we'll accidentally consider failover healthy.
jon: Add metrics and trace tags: residency.failover.rejected, residency.failover.routed, trace tag residency.failover=true + tenant_hash.
ops-bot: chaos-svc: Chaos run scheduled tomorrow 09:00 UTC to simulate eu region outage. @ken @devon @ashley
ken: I'll add a canary that simulates EU outage and assert that eu-pii tenants get 503 and other tenants route best-effort.
maria: Another surface: KV/cache hydration — we can't hydrate EU-residency keys into US cache. That would move PII.
devon: Suggest marking residency-sensitive cache keys with a residency tag and refusing cross-region hydrate. Three modes: copy (illegal), redirect (proxy to EU KV), deny (return miss + degrade). We should default to redirect -> but redirect still causes cross-region fetch; legal only forbids execution, not fetch? need legal check.
ashley: Legal check: cross-region read of ephemeral model inputs is allowed only if data is pseudonymized. Assume we must deny unless tenant explicitly allowed cross-read. So default: deny/hard-miss -> degrade.
jon: I'll write an RFC follow-up to add tenant.residency_mode, cache residency enforcement, and a failover matrix mapping tenant sensitivity -> allowed actions. Will also add Console flags for tenant owners to set policy.
maria: Action items: jon -> RFC, devon -> PR for proxy rule & cache tagging, ken -> metrics + chaos canary, ashley -> update runbooks & confirm legal stance for cache reads. Please confirm by EOD.
ken: Confirmed. I'll try to get PR and canary ready by EOD. :thumbsup:
jon: RFC draft: https://rfc.internal/r/986-residency-failover (DRAFT) — feedback welcome.
maria: ACK. During chaos tests please triple-check we don't accidentally route EU-PII to US.
ops-bot: Reminder — incident playbook "region-failover" v2.1 will be used for tomorrow's exercise.
